Autocorrelation of the Residuals

Source: R/plot_diagnostic.R
plot_acf.Rd

Selects the graph of the sample autocorrelation of the quantile residuals, or of their squares, in the order of the observations, with the limits \(\pm 1.96/\sqrt{n}\).

Usage

plot_acf(lag_max = 30, squared = FALSE, seed = NULL)

Arguments

lag_max

The largest lag.

squared

Whether to use the squared residuals.

seed

A single number that seeds the randomization, or NULL.

Value

A PlotAcf object, inheriting from diagnostic_plot.

Details

The autocorrelations are those of stats::acf() at the lags 1 to lag_max. Under a correct model with independent observations the quantile residuals are independent standard normal variables, the autocorrelations have standard deviation near \(1/\sqrt{n}\), and about five percent of them fall outside the limits. The autocorrelation of the squares (squared = TRUE) detects a variance that depends on the past. The order is the row order of the data, so the graph is meaningful for a series, or for data sorted within a panel; for a discrete family the residuals are randomized and seed makes them reproducible.

See also

plot_residuals(), diagnostics()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(t = 1:150)
dd$y <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.5), n = 150))
fit <- statmod(y ~ 1, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, type = plot_acf(lag_max = 20))
